note: Book 3, step 1: the 8 prefectures of cpu-prefecture-capitals-lora.json, now scoring only the capital's tokens ("score" in examples/prefecture-capitals-train.jsonl: 22 scored positions instead of 118). Sweep: train-text --lora 8 at lr 1e-4 / 3e-4 / 1e-3 x 30 / 100 / 300 steps, and the full FFN once (lr 3e-6, 100 steps). Each run measured by lens-batch --generate 16 over the 47 prefectures and the 8 paraphrases, compared with the untrained student by tools/compare_capitals.py (groups: examples/prefecture-capitals-split.json), and train-eval on the first 512 tokens of README.md. Result: the trained facts are learned, but as a set of answers, not as a mapping. From 100 steps at lr 1e-4 (or 30 at 3e-4) every trained capital is top-1 at the forced position (8/8), and free answers reach 6/8 (LoRA) or 7/8 (full FFN). But every other prefecture now answers with one of the trained cities (mostly 仙台市, 高松市, 金沢市, 大津市): same-name guards forced right fall from 26/28 to 1-5/28, the 3 different-name prefectures already right to 0/3, and no held-out capital is learned. Free answers also drop the frame and start with the city. More steps or a higher lr only raise the README KL (0.04 -> 0.34). The full FFN at lr 3e-6 keeps the KL at 0.014 and learns the paraphrases (8/8 forced), with the same collapse. With only correct answers for the trained 8, nothing in the loss ties the city to the prefecture: raising those 8 cities' logits everywhere lowers it. So held-out conclusions need negatives: step 2 adds replay pairs of other prefectures' own capitals.
